description: Comet Code is a team of passionate developers and innovators participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We're tackling “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” by analyzing NASA data to discover environmental trends and present insights through interactive visualizations. We're looking for teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, data science, statistics, web development, Earth science, and UI/UX. Let's collaborate and build something impactful!
summary: ORBITAL is an interactive digital museum exploring the human-made machines and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon and Mars. Created in response to NASA's "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, ORBITAL transforms mission histories and scientific records into an immersive space archaeology experience. Visitors can discover historic landers, rovers, and instruments through curated storytelling, interactive artifact exploration, planetary environments, and guidance from a virtual museum curator, Dr. Mae Vance. By connecting each artifact to the mission it served and the science it enabled, ORBITAL helps school-age space enthusiasts understand that exploration does not end when a mission does. Every machine left behind carries a story of human curiosity, engineering, and discovery.
details:
ORBITAL is an interactive digital museum designed to make the history of human exploration beyond Earth accessible, engaging, and educational. It focuses on the Moon and Mars, presenting selected historic spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments through an immersive museum experience.

Visitors can explore curated artifact collections, discover mission histories, examine available 3D models, and interact with planetary environments. The experience combines historical imagery, scientific information, artifact-specific storytelling, and guided narration from Dr. Mae Vance, a virtual museum curator.

The project emphasizes the stories behind the hardware: why each machine was built, what it accomplished, what scientific knowledge it contributed, and why it remains on another world. It also distinguishes equipment deliberately left behind from machines whose missions ended or whose hardware was lost or damaged.

ORBITAL aims to turn mission archives into an accessible learning experience for students and space enthusiasts, encouraging curiosity about planetary science, engineering, and the history of exploration.

The application was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Zustand, GSAP, and Framer Motion. NASA mission information, imagery, planetary resources, and 3D assets are incorporated where applicable.

Its creative approach is to present space archaeology as an explorable digital museum rather than a conventional collection of articles or static mission summaries.
